name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz restricted; new mine claim 13 Nov
summary: Iran says a gas carrier hit a mine east of Hormuz on 13 Nov; JMIC rates the strait severe, transits far below 2025
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a gas carrier hit a mine and exploded east of the Strait of Hormuz on 13 Nov after using an unauthorised route; the claim is unverified. JMIC recorded four tanker attacks on 10–11 Nov, rates the strait's threat level severe and puts daily transits in single digits to low double digits, against about 138 a day in 2025 (Safety4Sea, 13 Nov). UKMTO counted traffic about 65% below pre-conflict levels in the week to 10 Nov (Gulf News), and a senior Iranian lawmaker told Euronews on 6 Nov the standoff over the strait was not sustainable.
for_you: Gulf oil, LNG and LPG cargoes face attack risk, delays and higher insurance costs, which tends to feed through to fuel and energy prices. Travellers and seafarers in the region should follow FCDO travel advice and UKMTO guidance.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded: daily transits single digits to low double digits vs ~138/day in 2025 (Alert)

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
